title: The integral constructible category and its heart
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell$ be a prime different from $p$, and let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Coefficients are the completed ring sheaf $R_X=\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and the ambient category is the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use the constructibility and bounded constructibility of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the standard truncations of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and the fixed-universe size convention [def-weil-size-convention].

1. $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is a full triangulated subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Its objects are bounded, and it is stable under the standard truncations.
2. $\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ identifies with the objects of $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ concentrated in degree $0$. It is an abelian full subcategory of $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$: kernels and cokernels of its morphisms, computed in $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$, belong to it. It is closed under extensions and essentially small (its isomorphism classes form a set in the chosen universe).

proof.text: Finite type over a field and quasi-compactness make X Noetherian. Shrink the arbitrary-universe finite extension and lift it to the scheme universe. Its spectral valuation ring is isometrically isomorphic to the original small valuation ring, hence the corresponding continuous-function condensed ring objects are isomorphic. Transport constant-model constructibility along this coefficient isomorphism and apply the integral local finite-presentation comparison. Thus the constant-model predicate equals the stratified locally finitely presented predicate on the same module category.

The continuous integers equal the spectral valuation integers. Integral constructible weak Serre closure therefore transfers through the predicate equality: zero, ambient kernels, cokernels and extensions are constant-model constructible. Cohomology in this weak Serre class is triangulated, as is its intersection with the bounded part of the standard t-structure. Both truncations have the original cohomology in the surviving degrees and zero elsewhere; their upper and lower bounds follow from the standard t-structure truncation instances.

The single functor is fully faithful, and its degree-zero homology is the original module while its other homology is zero. A bounded constant-model complex concentrated in degree zero is isomorphic to a single complex and its degree-zero module satisfies the predicate. This gives exactly the claimed essential image. Split extensions give finite biproducts; together with ambient kernel and cokernel closure this makes the full subcategory abelian by the Mathlib abelian-subcategory instance.

Apply the proved essential-smallness theorem for constructible module objects to the pulled-back coefficient ring on the compact locally Noetherian scheme X. Transport its object-property essential smallness across the equality of predicates from step 1, and use the standard full-subcategory instance. This also covers empty X.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs (1)-(2); shorter weak-Serre proof and direct constructible-module smallness, formalized by Z8

blueprint_update.statement:
1. $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is a triangulated subcategory of
   $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ whose objects are bounded, stable under
   the standard truncations.
2. $\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the objects of $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ concentrated
   in degree $0$, is an abelian subcategory of
   $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$: kernels and cokernels of morphisms
   in it, computed in $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$, lie in it. It is
   closed under extensions and essentially small.

proof.text:
(1) Derived completeness is stable under shifts and cones: $K$ is derived
complete if and only if
$R\varprojlim(\cdots\xrightarrow{\pi_E}K\xrightarrow{\pi_E}K)=0$, and this
derived limit is an exact functor of $K$. Reduction modulo $\pi_E$ is exact, so constructibility of the
reduction is stable under shifts and cones because bounded constructible
complexes on the étale site form a triangulated subcategory. Hence
$\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is triangulated. Its objects are bounded: by
[det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model](1) each of the finitely many strata,
being quasi-compact, is covered by finitely many charts on which the object is a
bounded complex of finite free modules. Stability under truncation is
[det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model](3).

(2) Let $\varphi:C\to C'$ be a morphism in $\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ with cone
$D\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Then $\ker\varphi=H^{-1}(D)$ and
$\operatorname{coker}\varphi=H^0(D)$, which lie in $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by
[det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model](2) and are in degree $0$. So
$\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is an abelian subcategory. An extension
$0\to C'\to C\to C''\to0$ of modules gives a distinguished triangle
$C'\to C\to C''\to C'[1]$; if the ends are constructible, so is $C$ by (1).
Essential smallness: a constructible sheaf is determined up to isomorphism by
a finite stratification of $X$, finite presentations of
$\mathcal O_E$-modules giving local models on a pro-étale cover taken from a
fixed small site, and gluing morphisms; these data form a set.
